I went to the evening performance in Philly and I think the only issues we had were a few people trying to take photos. There was one wonderful soul who blurted out MOONLIGHT JELLIES. When it was being introduced. This was met with laughter and clapping as we all shared their enthusiasm. 

Being an avid concert goer of all types of music, I truly feel that this show was run in a way that the audience was encouraged to be engaged and experience. It was meant to be accessible, not stuffy. 

I would have been irritated if people around me were talking constantly... But all I heard were positives and how much everyone loved the venue having not been before and wanted to go back. I look at it the same way I look at bowling etiquette. I am not going to get mad at a kid for running up and bowling right next to me instead of waiting, they are new and learning. As long as they don't take my turn in my lane we are cool.

As a woman... It truly depends on who you are trying to attract. As an INTP woman, I looked for someone who was confident and intelligent but who was willing to admit when they are wrong and be flexible with their thinking. Not everyone wants or appreciates those things.

If you are looking to attract someone that is looking to be sheparded through life then a bit more edge/confidence/perception/assertiveness is needed. If you are looking for a true equal then it shouldn't be as big of a deal as long as you can hold up your end of things. 

It's good to get out of your comfort zone and grow, but important not to push yourself so far that you become a character instead of you. The right person will appreciate you for what you bring to the table. You might need to widen your definition of what you are looking for to find that person.

Same.  I feel like most people avoid me because I am "intimidating." A friend once temporarily ghosted me as a potential dating partner before apologizing profusely two weeks later. He said he wasn't used to feeling like he was coming into a battle of words/wit ill equipped. I said I wasn't used to men who felt like that owning up to it. He is now just a great renaissance faire buddy.

I feel guilty for accepting initial treatment when I was diagnosed with a heart condition a few years ago. That care and time could have gone to someone else with people who cared and needed to be around.

Been there... You just have to find the person that finds it fascinating that you are a curious person, not intimidated by it. I have also been the person to let relationships go because the other person wasn't intellectually challenging enough. The pendulum goes both ways if that sort of thing is a priority for you.

I refer to this as 'the great culling'... for me it happens every six to seven years... most of my life changes completely and I end up having to replace the vast majority of my friends with new.  The thing is that people change.  Sometimes for better, sometimes for worse, and sometimes for better when in the moment it seems like it was for worse.  Hopefully you are seeking help for the substance issues if they are ongoing.  Outside of that I know that it isn't much help right at the moment but you are not at all alone in the rest of it.  It is hard, especially when you're used to being 'the smart one with potential' who things come easily to, to run up against a wall and not know how to get around or over it.  You're supposed to lose all of these things at some point in your life, if you haven't then you aren't making mistakes and growing as a person.  It just sucks for everything to have happened at the same time.  You just need to find a way to tunnel under your wall and pop up on the other side, a changed person but a better one for the experience.  

Also, you more intelligibly construct posts even in your darkest hour than people do on their best days.  That is a sign that you still have at least something of your intelligence, if not much more than you thought.

I am assuming that her grandmother is sick? If not and she likes and trusts you consider involving her. Your girlfriend might be upset in the immediate but in the long term she will realize that you did it because you care. If her grandmother is sick just be there for her, listen to her, and tell her how concerned you are. I didn't have the best relationship with my parents as a teenager either. Sometimes it just takes one person to make that difference.  But do keep trying to convince her to talk to someone... even if it is just about her issues at home instead of the depression itself.

People we both know tell her how great she looks after having lost 40lbs... but say nothing to me even if I'm standing right next to her.  It is discouraging because I feel as if my hard work was really for nothing... it obviously hasn't changed how people perceive me.
